rationale: A unanimous Court is most likely to reverse on narrow Skilling/lenity/fair-notice grounds, holding the Second Circuit’s “reliance-and-control” instruction too indeterminate to define a fiduciary duty for a private citizen absent objective indicia like formal office, delegation, or agency. Roberts is best positioned to keep the opinion institutionally modest, while Gorsuch (lenity/separation of powers) and Barrett (administrable limiting principle) are the most likely concurrence writers if they want sharper constraints.
